links.outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot responses when queries repeated 1 week later
links.effect: ChatGPT showed the greatest consistency (89.7% reproducibility); the abstract notes inconsistencies across chatbots.
links.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated the greatest consistency (89.7% reproducibility) and provided no misleading content.

links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of chatbot clinical knowledge on FMF, including diagnosis
links.effect: Comprehensive/correct responses: Gemini 87.7%, Grok 83.6%, ChatGPT 81.6%; Grok gave 4.0% misleading responses, mainly on diagnosis; diagnostic performance notably lower.
links.quote: Grok was the only model to produce misleading responses (4.0%), primarily in diagnosis-related answers.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, comprehensiveness, and consistency of three LLM chatbots answering patient-focused medical questions on Familial Mediterranean Fever using expert evaluation.
